questions.a: One named and standing: 'shim start' is one identifiable event in either order of the bus ticket (registration into the bus process, or BaseShim.__init__ today). Load-bearing only for where the lines sit, not for the behaviour; the falsifier tooth 4 (check in exactly one place, the base) holds either way.

One point not wrapped at /intent, now wrapped: what the shim does when the spawn itself fails (no user manager, systemd unreachable). Answer: the superclaude launcher's fall-through (setsid spawn, and the log line SAYS it will die with the caller) is reused verbatim; the shim logs the same three outcomes. Nothing else asserted-wrapped is open.

Consulted the lab. ground_loop charter: 'any entry point gains the only-once guarantee by spawning the runner — a CALL, not a policy' — this is one more caller, same call. launchers charter's superclaude spawn: both call the guarded runner, so both may exist until the shim path is proven; then the launcher's spawn retires (recorded as this ticket's what_dies-later, not now). Akien's bound on the loop's contents (pulse, flags, devices-found list, ever) is untouched by construction. No Law collides.

A Haiku-level builder needs: (a) where — cairn/tools/base/shim.py, the start/registration path, one function `ensure_ground_loop(now)`; (b) the read — `liveness.read_liveness(now)['verdict'] == 'DEAD'` from cairn.devices.cairn.machines.ground_loop.liveness, never pgrep; (c) the spawn — copy the systemd-run block from launchers/superclaude (unit cairn-ground-loop, SuccessExitStatus=3, --setenv HOME and PATH, append redirects to ~/.cairn/logs/ground_loop_nohup.log) and its fall-through; (d) the proof — set HOME to a scratch instance, assert DEAD→LIVE and the diff-stat tooth; (e) don't — no import of the loop's runner as a library (spawn the module), no sleep-poll for LIVE beyond one beat (1s ruled cadence). All written into the ticket's how.
